title: Bulbul
aiNote: This app was built with heavy AI-assisted coding. That said, great care has been taken in the quality and delivery of the final product.
description: Bulbul is a tray-resident push-to-talk voice dictation app for Windows, built end-to-end as a v1.0.0 public release. Hold the hotkey, speak, release — Groq Whisper transcribes, an app-aware LLM cleans the text up based on which app you're dictating into, and the polished result is pasted at the cursor. The core engineering challenge wasn't transcription — Whisper handles that — it was making the desktop wrapper invisible: 2.7 MB resident memory (~100x lighter than Electron-based competitors like Wispr Flow), instant hotkey response, and zero idle CPU.
shortDescription: Push-to-talk voice dictation for Windows at 2.7 MB resident — ~100x lighter than Wispr Flow. Hold a key, speak, release; polished text lands in any app.
features: Tiny Footprint: Runs at 2.7 MB resident memory — ~100x lighter than Electron-based competitors like Wispr Flow — by using WebView2 instead of bundling Chromium, deferring window rendering until the dashboard is opened, and keeping a single-process Rust backend.

Zero-Idle Audio Pipeline: Global push-to-talk hotkey → 16 kHz mono PCM capture via cpal (Whisper's smallest accepted payload) → streamed directly to Groq with no disk writes → LLM cleanup → clipboard paste. The mic only opens while the key is held, so CPU and memory stay flat between dictations.

App-Aware LLM Cleanup: Detects the foreground process via Win32 GetForegroundWindow + QueryFullProcessImageNameW, maps it to one of 35+ categorized apps with an O(1) HashMap lookup, and swaps the system prompt per category so tone matches the venue (chat for Slack, formal for Outlook, bullets for docs).

Correction-Memory System (V3.1): User-defined fixes are applied as direct pre-cleanup string substitutions instead of LLM few-shot examples — sidestepping the 8B model's tendency to echo example fixes, eliminating per-dictation token cost, and cutting cleanup latency.

Signed Mode-B Auto-Update: minisign-verified releases via GitHub Actions (tauri-action), background download on a 6-hour cadence with the Update handle stashed in memory for sub-second install-on-quit, plus a non-blocking in-app update banner.

Privacy-First Telemetry: Opt-out, append-only event log buffered in memory and flushed on size (10 events) or a 30s timer to Supabase PostgREST under INSERT-only Row-Level Security — durable anon UUID, zero PII, no IP retention, and never blocks a user-facing action.

Tray-First Lifecycle: tauri-plugin-autostart (start with Windows by default), hidden-window startup, and a tray-driven Quit that installs pending updates on exit — cold-start RAM stays under 3 MB until the dashboard is opened.

Release Engineering: Code-signed NSIS installer, GitHub Actions release workflow, structured issue/discussion templates, README/CHANGELOG/CONTRIBUTING/SmartScreen FAQ, and an MIT-licensed public repo.

title: SilkHR
highlight: 1st Prize — Rumik × AWS Voice AI Hackathon 2026. Built in under 6 hours during the live event, against the rest of the cohort.
description: SilkHR is a two-sided AI voice interview platform built to fix three problems with existing tools: they sound robotic, they can't handle the English-Hindi code-switching most Indian engineers actually speak, and they aren't available to candidates for practice. Recruiters build interview templates, bulk-assign candidates by email, review scored transcripts, and explicitly release results (held by default); candidates take scheduled screens in-browser or run unlimited ad-hoc mock interviews tailored to any role. The centerpiece is a streaming voice pipeline — Deepgram Nova-3 STT → Gemini Flash → Silk muga TTS — that drove per-turn latency from 11–17s down to ~2.4s by streaming on both ends and keeping clients warm across HMR.
shortDescription: Two-sided AI voice interviewer with native Hinglish, real follow-ups, and a streaming Deepgram → Gemini → Silk muga pipeline at ~2.4s per turn. 1st prize, Rumik × AWS Voice AI Hackathon.
features: Two-Sided Platform: Recruiters build interview templates, bulk-assign candidates by email, review scored transcripts, and explicitly release results (held by default); candidates take scheduled interviews in-browser or run unlimited ad-hoc mock interviews tailored to any role.
Native Hinglish, No Toggle: Deepgram Nova-3 STT runs with language 'multi' so the interviewer handles the English-Hindi code-switching Indian engineers actually speak — no language switch required.
Recruiter-Grade Brain: Gemini Flash prompted to behave like an Indian recruiter — short conversational lines, adaptive deep follow-ups, and a pressure mode.
Emotion TTS: Silk muga streams PCM at 24kHz with first audio under a second, played gaplessly through a single shared AudioContext that schedules incoming chunks back-to-back.

Streaming Voice Pipeline: Cut per-turn latency from 11–17s (REST-only v1) to ~2.4s by streaming STT live, minting Silk WS tokens server-side, opening the TTS WebSocket from the browser, and keeping Mongo + model clients warm across HMR.
Release-Gated Results Flow: Templates → bulk assignments → sessions → recruiter-released feedback, secured with httpOnly-cookie auth.

title: Spktr
description: Spktr is a desktop AI assistant that watches your screen, answers questions about what's currently visible, and proactively alerts you when it detects notable issues like errors, failed builds, or warning prompts. It's built as a Tauri 2 desktop app with a Next.js overlay UI, a Node/Express backend, and a Rust host that manages the native window, system tray, global shortcut, and sidecar lifecycle. It captures the screen periodically, skips unchanged frames with perceptual-hash diffing, streams answers token-by-token, and layers in long-term vector memory plus per-session context so the assistant gets sharper the more you use it.
shortDescription: Desktop AI assistant (Tauri 2 + Rust) that watches your screen, answers questions about what's visible, and proactively flags errors and failed builds — with sqlite-vec long-term memory and per-session context.
features: Screen-Aware Q&A: Captures the screen every ~7s, skips unchanged frames via sharp-based perceptual-hash diffing, and answers questions about what's currently visible — streamed token-by-token to the overlay over SSE.

Proactive Engine: On meaningful screen changes (>5% pHash diff, 90s cooldown), a meta-model returns a structured { shouldIntervene, suggestion } decision and surfaces a dock toast that prefills the chat input — toggleable in Settings.

Long-Term Vector Memory: Extracts 1–3 reusable facts from every Q&A, embeds them at 768 dimensions, and retrieves the top-5 relevant memories via sqlite-vec native KNN (with automatic JS cosine fallback) to inject into every prompt.
Session Context: Tracks interactions per session (15-minute inactivity timeout), compresses them to an AI summary every 20 interactions, and injects current-session context at the top of each prompt.
Four-Layer Prompt Assembly: Each prompt is built from session context → recent history (last 5 Q&A in 30 min) → top-5 long-term memories → current screenshot.
Pluggable Providers: An OpenAI-compatible client layer supporting Ollama and LM Studio (local) or Groq (cloud), with guided onboarding, connectivity tests, and hot-reload on config change.

Native Desktop Host: A Rust/Tauri 2 host manages the floating overlay (Ctrl+Shift+Space), system tray, and global shortcut, and launches the backend as a bundled sidecar that's killed when the app exits.
prerequisites: A model provider: Ollama, LM Studio, or Groq

title: Smart Airport Ride-Pooling Backend
description: A production-ready backend API for airport ride pooling that intelligently matches passengers into shared rides while guaranteeing zero double-bookings under high concurrency. It uses an O(n) PostGIS geospatial matching algorithm with composite scoring to minimize detours (under 30%), PostgreSQL pessimistic and optimistic locking for ACID-safe seat allocation, and multi-layer caching plus connection pooling to scale to 10,000+ concurrent users — load-tested at 562 req/s with 88ms average latency and a 0% error rate.
shortDescription: Production-ready Node.js + PostGIS API that pools airport rides with zero double-bookings, scaling to 10,000+ concurrent users at 562 req/s.
features: Smart Matching Algorithm: Linear O(n) scan with early termination cuts candidates by 88%, scored on a composite of detour (50%), distance (30%), and capacity (20%) to keep shared-ride detours under 30%.
Zero Double-Bookings: Pessimistic locking via SELECT FOR UPDATE plus optimistic version-field locking inside ACID transactions eliminates race conditions under concurrent load.
High Concurrency: Scales to 10,000+ concurrent users — load-tested at 562 req/s with 88ms average latency, 209ms P99, and a 0% error rate.
Performance Optimization: Multi-layer caching (70% query reduction), connection pooling (7x speedup), and B-Tree/composite indexing (10–100x faster queries).
Geospatial Matching: PostGIS-powered geographic queries with a 10km search radius and GIST spatial indexing on cab locations.
Dynamic Pricing: Distance-based fare (₹50 base + ₹10/km) with pooling discounts for shared rides and a Redis-ready surge-pricing framework.
Production-Ready Infrastructure: Dockerized with Docker Compose, an autocannon load-testing suite, schema migration and seed scripts, and a Postman API collection.

title: JobBoard AI
description: A conversational, AI-driven job aggregator that turns "find me remote Python internships" into a ranked shortlist of real openings. Instead of filling out search forms across a dozen job sites, users just chat — an LLM parses the request into structured intent, the backend fans out concurrent fetchers across 6+ job boards, cross-source duplicates are collapsed, and every result is scored by an LLM against the user's actual preferences, surfacing the best matches with per-dimension reasoning.
shortDescription: Conversational AI job search — describe what you want in plain English and an LLM pipeline fetches across 6+ boards, then deduplicates, scores, and ranks the best matches.
features: Natural-Language Search: An LLM (Llama 3.3 70B via Groq) parses free-form queries into structured intent — role, tech stack, seniority, and location — so users find jobs by chatting instead of filling out forms.

Parallel Multi-Source Ingestion: Concurrent async fetchers fan out across 6+ job boards (LinkedIn, Indeed, Google, Glassdoor via JobSpy, RemoteOK, Hacker News), each isolated to its own DB session to eliminate SQLAlchemy concurrency races, with wall-clock timeouts so one slow source never blocks the request.

Cross-Source Deduplication: SHA-256 fingerprinting with title/company normalization and canonical job-board ID extraction collapses the same role posted on multiple boards into a single card, keeping the richest copy.

Cost-Efficient LLM Scoring: Batch-of-5 scoring with a concurrency semaphore, exponential-backoff retry on rate limits (429), and single-job fallback — cutting token cost ~5x while scoring skills, seniority, and location (0–100 each) with a one-sentence rationale.

Freshness-Aware Ranking: Re-ranks by an effective score that blends the raw LLM match score with an exponential time-decay curve, plus a deterministic pre-LLM seniority title filter so an intern query never wastes budget scoring "Principal Engineer" roles.
Resilient Streaming Chat: Fresh Clerk JWTs minted per backend call survive 30s+ pipeline runs, with optimistic UI updates and abortable streams.

Monetization & Admin: Per-user search quotas across free / trial / unlimited plan tiers, plus an admin console for user management, access restriction, and plan grants — integrated with the Clerk user API.

title: AuthentiTest

The application leverages AWS Rekognition for real-time face verification, Groq API for AI-generated content and plagiarism analysis, and integrates seamlessly with MongoDB for data persistence.

title: TP-Link Campus Identity
description: An identity-based network security system for campuses that uses a student's admission number as the security boundary instead of physical location. It integrates with TP-Link Omada infrastructure to automatically assign VLANs and control network access based on who you are, not where you connect — the core idea being "WHO you are determines network access, not WHERE you connect." A single admission number controls access across all campus systems, with automatic role-based VLAN assignment and complete identity-correlated audit trails.
shortDescription: Zero-trust campus network where identity (admission number) — not location — controls access. Integrates with TP-Link Omada for automatic role-based VLAN assignment via RADIUS + Keycloak SSO.
features: Identity-Centric Zero Trust: Access is controlled by verified admission numbers rather than physical location — 'WHO you are determines network access, not WHERE you connect' — with role-based VLAN assignment for students, faculty, and admins, and complete identity-correlated audit trails.
Network Access Control: RADIUS protocol integration with TP-Link Omada dynamically assigns VLANs by user role, with real-time session management and monitoring.
Single Sign-On: Keycloak-backed OAuth2/OIDC SSO across campus portals (LMS, Library, Admin) gives users automatic network access with no manual configuration.
Real-Time Admin Console: Approve or block users with instant network impact, monitor live sessions with identity tracking, and manage accounts through Keycloak integration.
Omada Hardware Integration: Designed for TP-Link EAP660 HD / EAP245 access points, TL-SG3428 managed VLAN switches, an ER7206 VPN router, and OC200/OC300 Omada controllers.
Per-User Policy: Dynamic VLAN assignment and per-user bandwidth control enforced at the network edge.
prerequisites: Keycloak configured with campus realm settings
